subject: Electronic Signs Ordinance - 10 March Planning Commission Meeting
comment: Hi All, Attached is the Provo City Planning Commission Staff Report regarding the proposed amendments to the Provo City ordinances regulating electronic signs. Please note that the Planning Commission Meeting is Wednesday 10 March at 6:00 pm. My previous email was incorrect for the date! The ordinance is scheduled for a hearing before the Provo City Municipal Council on Tuesday 16 March at 5:30 pm, depending on the outcome from the Planning Commission meeting. Information on how to participate in the virtual meetings is copied below. The four issues I will be pursuing are: 1. The North University Avenue Design Corridor restricts signs to a maximum size of 60 square feet and a maximum height of 10 feet above sidewalk grade. This restriction must remain. 2. The ordinance does not address the placement of electronic signs on commercial property adjacent to residential property. Transitions and buffers between adjacent properties with differing use are typical. One possible “buffer” is a “lights out” provision turning signs off between 10 PM and 7 AM, a time frame used in noise ordinance restrictions. 3. Provide for a live demonstration of the maximum light intensity above ambient lighting permitted by ordinance and demonstrate intensities above and below the proposed maximum limit. 4. Will the Planning Commission act as enabled by 14.38.010 (7) to order the correction or removal of the sign at the Esquire Building (3000 North University Avenue). The sign was erected without Planning Commission approval as evidenced by the lack of a building permit issued by Provo City Building Inspection. When a sign is erected or maintained contrary to code, the Planning Commission is empowered to order the removal of the sign or the correction of the sign within a time period not exceeding 30 days. All are invited to participate as schedule and interest allow. Cheers, R. Paul Evans

subject: In regards to Planning Mtg of 3/10/21
comment: Please consider the following when making your recommendations to the city council. Does anyone approving these electronic signs in Provo ever look on a map to see where the residential zones are? We have strict codes for lighting in residential zones but somehow if you are adjacent to a business zone, those residential considerations are completely ignored. In the case of the two illegal signs located at 3000 N. University and 3152 N. University, both businesses were built and operated decades after the homes were established. A picture is worth a thousand words. Please look at these and consider whether you would like to have electronic signs installed in your backyard. And that is the smaller sign at 3000 N. University. The bigger sign at Blue Rock Medical is worse. This is like living on the Las Vegas Strip. If you insist on allowing these garish signs to pollute Provo, could you at least pass a light ban between 10 pm to 7 am for those signs within sight of a residential neighborhood? Thank you, Marilyn Steffensen

subject: USA & ISA recommendations sign ordinance amendments item #1 Planning Commission Agenda -

Please see our attached recommendations along with supporting documentation. Do not hesitate to contact me with any questions.
